page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 16 physical cores on a shared Intel Xeon 6448H processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system features 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core, and includes a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in specific data-processing and machine learning tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 35.53 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 15.59 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 173.77 GB/sec for read operations and 66.7 GB/sec for write operations. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier capabilities, processing 13631.52 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 6293.73 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

While the GPU and memory subsystems deliver high-tier performance for AI workloads, the shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed result in average multi-core CPU performance, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core score of 34834.61 and PassMark CPU score of 40930.36. This hardware profile offers high resource density for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated tasks without the cost of dedicated CPU instances. The server is suited for LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated data processing.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server designed for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated workloads. It features 16 physical cores on a shared Intel Xeon 6448H processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 180.0 GB of system memory and a 1200 GB NVMe SSD. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in large language model inference, reaching 6293.73 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 7B model, alongside top-tier single-threaded compression speeds. However, the shared CPU allocation delivers average multi-core performance. This configuration represents a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial VRAM and system memory, such as LLM inference, machine learning, and data science pipelines, without requiring dedicated CPU resources.
